Explanation of the words:

﴿Sabbih is-ma rabbika al-a'la﴾: That is, declare the name of your Lord free of any defect, that it be named by other than Him, or mentioned with mockery or play. It should only be mentioned with reverence and glorification. And declare your Lord free of what is not befitting to Him, such as association (shirk), a consort, a son, a likeness, or an equal.

al-A'la (the Most High): That is, above everything and dominant over everything.

alladhi khalaqa fa-sawwa (Who created and proportioned): That is, He created man and proportioned his limbs by making them harmonious and without disproportion.

wa-alladhi qaddara fa-hada (Who measured and guided): That is, He measured what He willed for whomever He willed, and guided him to carry out what He had decreed for him and upon him.

wa-alladhi akhraja al-mar'a (Who brought forth the pasture): That is, He caused the grass and herbage to grow.

fa-ja'alahu ghutha'an ahwa (And made it a dark stubble): That is, after its greenness and freshness, it became dry, black, crumbled debris.

sanuqri'uka fa-la tansa (We shall make you recite, so you will not forget): That is, the Qur'an, so that you will not forget it, by Our permission.

illa ma sha'a Allah (Except what Allah wills): That is, except what We will to make you forget, for you will forget it. This is when Allah, exalted is He, wills to abrogate something of the Qur'an in its wording; then His Messenger ﷺ is made to forget it.

wa-nuyassiruka li-l-yusra (And We will ease you toward ease): That is, toward the easy Sharia, which is Islam.

fa-dhakkir in nafa'at al-dhikra (So remind, if the reminder benefits): That is, whether the one who is reminded is benefited or not, and "reminding" means admonishing with the Qur'an.

wa-yatajannabuha (And the one who avoids it): That is, avoids the reminder, leaving it aside and paying it no heed.

al-ashqa (The most wretched): That is, the disbeliever whose wretchedness was written from eternity.

yasla al-nar al-kubra (Who will enter the greatest Fire): That is, the Fire of the Hereafter.

la yamutu fihā wa-la yahya (In which he will neither die nor live): That is, he will not die and thus find rest, nor live and thus find comfort.

Meaning of the verses:

Allah's saying ﴿Sabbih is-ma rabbika al-a'la﴾: This is a command from Allah to His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, and his community follows him in it, to declare the name of his Lord free of being named by other than Him, or being mentioned in a filthy place, or being mentioned without reverence and respect. These are five verses: the first contains the command to declare Allah's name free of defect, and the four after it are about making Him known, may He be glorified and exalted, so that His name is magnified and His essence is exalted, and He is far removed from partners, consorts, and offspring. Allah's saying ﴿sanuqri'uka fa-la tansa﴾ is a promise from Allah to His Messenger. Its cause was perhaps that when Jibril brought him the verses, he feared forgetting them, so he would hasten to recite them before Jibril, peace be upon him, had finished dictating them to him, and this caused him hardship; so his Lord reassured him that he would not forget what Jibril recited to him. ﴿illa ma sha'a Allah﴾: that He should cause him to forget it, for a wisdom that required it; then he would forget it. Allah's saying ﴿wa-nuyassiruka li-l-yusra﴾: that is, toward the easy path free of hardship, which is the Islamic Sharia, built on the foundation that there is no hardship in religion: ﴿wa-ma ja'ala 'alaykum fi al-din min haraj﴾ [al-Hajj: 78]. Allah's saying ﴿fa-dhakkir in nafa'at al-dhikra﴾: whether you have despaired of their faith or not, the reminder benefits or does not; for he, ﷺ, is commanded to convey, so he conveys to the disbeliever and the believer, and reminds both. The command is over. Allah's saying ﴿sayadhdhakkaru man yakhsha﴾: that is, whoever fears Allah's punishment, through his faith in Him and knowledge of Him, will be reminded and admonished. ﴿wa-yatajannabuha﴾: that is, the reminder. ﴿al-ashqa﴾: that is, the most wretched of the two groups, the group that is reminded and the group that is not. ﴿alladhi yasla al-nar al-kubra﴾: that is, he enters the greatest Fire, the Fire of the Day of Resurrection. ﴿thumma la yamutu fiha﴾: from the torment of it, so he may rest; ﴿wa-la yahya﴾: so that he may find ease and happiness, since wretchedness is bound to him. This is the state of the people of the Fire, and we seek refuge in Allah from the state of the people of the Fire.

3. The obligation to glorify with it in prostration, in every prostration of the prayer: "Subhana Rabbiya al-A'la" three times or more.

4. The legitimacy of reciting this surah in the witr prayer: in the first rak'ah one recites al-Fatiha and al-A'la; in the second, al-Fatiha and al-Kafirun; and in the witr rak'ah, al-Fatiha and al-Ikhlas or al-Ikhlas and the two protective surahs (al-Mu'awwidhatayn).

5. The Messenger ﷺ loved Surah al-A'la because it is the surah of his Lord, and because his Lord gave him two great glad tidings in it: first, that He would ease him toward ease, and for this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was never given a choice between two things without choosing the easier of them; and second, that He preserved him from forgetting by making him not forget. 2- Renunciation of the world and encouragement toward the Hereafter, because the world perishes and the Hereafter endures.

3- The agreement of the heavenly scriptures is evidence that they are revelation from God, whom He sent down upon His messengers, peace be upon them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 87, verses 14–19:

Explanation of the words:

Aflaḥa (أفلح): he succeeded, i.e., he won by being saved from the Fire and entering Paradise.

Man tazakkā (من تزكى): i.e., he purified himself through faith and righteous deeds after abandoning polytheism and sins.

Wa dhakara isma rabbihi (وذكر اسم ربه): i.e., at all times: when eating, when drinking, when sleeping, when the wind blows upon him, and in the prayer and outside the prayer, through glorification (tasbīḥ), praise (taḥmīd), declaration of God's oneness (tahlīl), and magnification (takbīr).

Fa-ṣallā (فصلى): i.e., the five daily prayers and the voluntary prayers, both the regular sunnah prayers and others.

Tu'thirūna (تؤثرون): i.e., you put forward and prefer the worldly life over the Hereafter.

Inna hādhā la-fī al-ṣuḥuf al-ūlā (إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى): i.e., this, namely His saying "He has succeeded who purified himself" up to His saying "and more lasting," is in the earlier scriptures.

Ṣuḥuf Ibrāhīm (صحف إبراهيم): as there were ten scrolls.

Wa Mūsā (وموسى): i.e., his Torah.

Meaning of the verses:

God, the Exalted, says: "He has succeeded who purified himself and remembered the name of his Lord and prayed." He informs that a believing servant who purifies his soul, i.e., cleanses it through faith and righteous deeds, and who remembers the name of his Lord at all times, is successful: at rising from sleep, at performing ablution, after ablution, during the prayer and after the prayer, when eating and drinking, and when dressing. Thus he is never without remembrance of God for an hour. He performs the five daily prayers and the voluntary prayers. The meaning of falāḥ (الفلاح) is success, and success is being saved from what is feared and attaining what is desired and loved. What is meant in the verse is being saved from the Fire and entering Paradise, as in the verse of Āl ʿImrān: "Whoever is turned away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has indeed succeeded" [3:185]. And His saying: "But you prefer the worldly life," O people, i.e., you prefer it over the Hereafter, so you work for it and forget the Hereafter, and send forward nothing for it. This is your nature, O people, except for one who remembers God and prays after having believed and been guided. Whereas the Hereafter is better than the world and more lasting: better in kind and more lasting in duration. Hence the wise said: "If the world were made of gold and the Hereafter of clay, the intelligent person would choose what remains over what perishes, because the world is transient and the Hereafter is everlasting." And His saying: "Indeed, this is in the earlier scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses" means that His saying "He has succeeded who purified himself" up to "better and more lasting" is mentioned in each of the scrolls of Abraham, which were ten, and in the scripture of Moses, the Torah.
